title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 365 (Order of dissolution of company)

content.overview: When the affairs of a company have been completely wound up, the Official Liquidator shall make an application to the Tribunal for dissolution of the company. The Tribunal shall thereupon order that the company be dissolved from the date of the order, and the company shall be dissolved accordingly. A copy of the order shall be forwarded within thirty days by the Official Liquidator to the Registrar, who shall record in the register that the company is dissolved.
content.glance: When affairs are completely wound up, Official Liquidator applies for dissolution; Tribunal orders dissolution from the date of the order; copy to Registrar within 30 days for recording.
content.study: Section 365 completes the Official Liquidator process. When the affairs of the company have been completely wound up, the Official Liquidator applies to the Tribunal for dissolution. The Tribunal orders that the company be dissolved from the date of the order. The Official Liquidator forwards a copy of the order to the Registrar within thirty days; the Registrar records in the register that the company is dissolved.

sections.heading: Dissolution order
sections.body: On complete winding up, Official Liquidator applies; Tribunal orders dissolution from date of order; copy to Registrar within 30 days for recording.

examples.title: Final dissolution
examples.body: After realisation and distribution in a summary liquidation, the Official Liquidator applies under s. 365; the Tribunal orders dissolution and the Registrar records it.

hypotheticals.question: From which date is the company dissolved under s. 365?
hypotheticals.analysis: From the date of the Tribunal’s order of dissolution.

misconceptions.trap: Dissolution is automatic when assets are exhausted.
misconceptions.correction: The Official Liquidator must apply and the Tribunal must order dissolution; the Registrar then records it.
